## How to Enable MMS on an iPhone


Did you know that iMessage is only one way to send texts with multimedia elements—like music, pictures, and videos—from your iPhone? A work-around is enabling Multimedia Messaging[Service](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/professional-services) (MMS) on your iPhone. This way, you can use MMS to send messages to friends, family, and even potential customers that are rich and meaningful. Sounds great, right?


Of course, to start sending MMS messages from your iPhone instead of iMessages, you need to enable MMS messaging. But with so many options to sift through from your iPhone’s settings, it’s easy to find yourself wondering: how do I enable MMS messaging?


If you’re trying to send a photo, video, or group text to an Android user and see an error saying "MMS messaging needs to be enabled," you just need to flip one setting on your iPhone.


Below, we'll cover what MMS is on iPhone, the exact steps to turn it on in the latest iOS, how it works alongside RCS and iMessage, and how to fix common MMS errors.


## What is MMS on iPhone?


MMS (Multimedia Messaging Service) on iPhone is a cellular carrier protocol that allows you to send photos, videos, audio clips, contact cards, and group messages to non-Apple devices (like Android phones) when iMessage or RCS is unavailable. Unlike iMessage—which runs over Apple's servers using Wi-Fi or mobile data—MMS relies on your wireless carrier's cellular network.


## Why is enabling MMS on iPhone important?


There are a lot of great reasons to enable MMS on your iPhone. As the name implies, MMS is a smarter and more convenient way to send multimedia assets from your phone because you can embed these assets within the messages themselves.


For example, if you send a URL to someone via MMS, you can embed metadata—such as an image, title, and subtitle—within the text itself. This makes it easier for[users to understand the message at a glance](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/user-authentication-identity/verify) .


More importantly, while iMessage offers the functionality of SMS and MMS, you can only send its messages to other iOS users. Enabling MMS on iPhone is a great way to send multimedia-enriched text to the largest number of people possible. Learn more about[what MMS is and how to deliver MMS messages](https://www.twilio.com/docs/glossary/what-is-mms) .


## How to enable MMS on iPhone


Often, your iPhone comes with MMS messaging already enabled by default. But if not, you might find yourself wondering: where are my MMS settings? If that sounds like you, or you’ve encountered a message that goes something like, “MMS messaging needs to be enabled to send this message.” Follow these steps to learn how to turn on MMS messages on your iPhone.


### 1. Open Settings


First, you’ll need to access your iPhone’s settings menu. Tap the Settings icon on your home screen, or swipe down on your home screen to pull up the search field, then type Settings and tap the result.


### 2. Tap Messages


From your settings screen, scroll down until you reach the label that reads Messages and tap it. If you have trouble finding it, look halfway down the section that starts with Passwords & Accounts.


### 3. Toggle MMS messaging on


Once you’re in the Messages menu, scroll down until you reach the SMS/MMS (or Text Messaging) section. Find MMS Messaging. If the toggle slider is to the left and grayed out, tap the toggle to send it right and turn it green. While you're here, make sure Send as Text Message (formerly Send as SMS) is also toggled on. Congratulations, you’ve just enabled MMS messaging for your iPhone!


If you don’t see the MMS messaging option, your carrier either doesn’t support MMS messaging on your plan or hasn't provisioned it on your SIM/eSIM—contact your wireless provider to enable it. Learn more about the[differences between SMS and MMS messages](https://www.twilio.com/learn/messaging/what-are-sms-and-mms) .


## MMS vs. RCS vs. iMessage on iPhone: What’s the difference?


Starting with iOS 18, Apple added support for[RCS (Rich Communication Services)](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/what-is-rcs-messaging) alongside iMessage and SMS/MMS. Understanding how all three work explains why you still need MMS enabled on your iPhone.


Messaging protocol


How it sends


When your iPhone uses it


iMessage


Wi-Fi or cellular data (Apple servers)


Messaging other iPhone, iPad, or Mac users


RCS


Wi-Fi or cellular data (carrier-supported)


Messaging Android users when both carriers and devices support RCS


MMS


Cellular data network only


Fallback for sending photos, videos, or group texts to non-Apple users when RCS isn't supported


Even with RCS enabled, keeping MMS Messaging turned on ensures your photos, videos, and group threads still go through when messaging older Android phones, contacts on carriers without RCS support, or mixed group chats.


## How to fix "MMS messaging needs to be enabled" on iPhone


If your iPhone displays the "MMS messaging needs to be enabled to send this message" alert, or fails to send a picture or group text to an Android contact, run through these five quick checks:


1. **Confirm MMS Messaging and Cellular Data are both ON:** MMS cannot travel over standard Wi-Fi alone. Go to Settings → Apps → Messages and verify that MMS Messaging is green. Then go to Settings → Cellular (or Mobile Service) and ensure Cellular Data is switched on.
2. **Check your active line (Dual SIM / eSIM users):** If you use two lines on your iPhone, go to Settings → Cellular, tap your primary texting line, and verify that Cellular Data and carrier settings are active for that specific number.
3. **Install pending carrier settings updates:** Go to Settings → General → About. If a carrier update is available, a pop-up prompt will appear—tap Update to refresh your network's MMS configuration.
4. **Toggle Airplane Mode or restart your iPhone:** Turn Airplane Mode on for 15 seconds, then turn it back off to force your iPhone to re-register with your carrier's MMS gateway.
5. **Contact your wireless carrier:** If the MMS Messaging toggle is completely missing from Settings → Apps → Messages, your carrier has likely disabled MMS provisioning on your account or SIM card and must re-enable it on their end.


## How to Disable Wi-Fi Calling


Some carriers will activate Wi-Fi-Calling on your iPhone by default which offers a better quality voice call when you are in an area with low cellular coverage. However, not all carriers support MMS when in Wifi-Calling mode. To disable Wifi-Calling on an iPhone, follow these steps.


### 1. Open Settings


As in the previous steps, let’s go back into the settings menu. Tap the Settings icon on your home screen or search.


### 2. Tap Mobile (or Mobile Service)


Tap Cellular (labeled Mobile Service or Mobile Data in some regions) to open your network configuration.


### 3. Tap Carrier Configuration


Under the SIMs section, tap on the phone line for the network provider you want to configure. If you have multiple SIMs or eSIM, you may have to do this multiple times.


### 4. Toggle Wi-Fi Calling off


Under the name of your network provider, find Wi-Fi Calling and if it is On, tap the arrow to enter the Wi-Fi Calling menu and toggle the slider to turn it Off.


After turning off Wi-Fi-Calling, you may want to turn off Wi-Fi and force your phone to use cellular data before turning Wi-Fi back on.


## Do you need to disable iMessage to send MMS?


No, you do not need to disable iMessage to send MMS messages. Your iPhone automatically uses iMessage (blue bubbles) for Apple-to-Apple chats and switches to RCS or MMS (green bubbles) when messaging Android or non-Apple users.


However, if you recently switched from an iPhone to an Android phone—or if a specific chat is stuck trying to send as a failed iMessage—you can temporarily turn off iMessage using these steps:


### 1. Open Settings


As with enabling MMS, disabling iMessage on your iPhone starts from your settings menu. Then, tap the Settings icon from your home screen, or swipe up to search for settings from the search field.


### 2. Tap Messages


Scroll to the bottom, tap Apps, and select Messages.


### 3. Toggle iMessage off


Find the iMessage label with the slider. If the toggle slider is green (On), tap the toggle to turn it off (gray).


## Troubleshooting common MMS issues on iPhone


**Q. My iPhone says “MMS messaging needs to be enabled.” What should I do?** Go to Settings → Apps → Messages and make sure MMS Messaging and Send as Text Message are both turned On, and confirm Cellular Data is enabled. If you don’t see the MMS option, your carrier may need to activate it—contact them for support.


**Q. Why can’t I send pictures or videos from my iPhone?** Large files may fail to send over MMS (most carriers cap MMS attachments between 1 MB and 3.5 MB). Try compressing the video or sending a smaller image. Also, make sure Cellular Data is turned On, as MMS won’t work over Wi-Fi alone for most carriers.


**Q. MMS worked before, but now it won’t send. How can I fix it?** Start by restarting your iPhone. Then check Settings → General → Software Update to install the latest iOS and carrier updates. You can also reset network settings under Settings → General → Transfer or Reset iPhone → Reset → Reset Network Settings.


**Q. MMS won’t send when Wi-Fi Calling is on.** Some carriers block MMS over Wi-Fi Calling. Turn off Wi-Fi Calling in Settings → Cellular → \[Your Line\] → Wi-Fi Calling, resend the message, and turn it back on if needed.

## Frequently asked questions


### What is MMS messaging on iPhone?


MMS (Multimedia Messaging Service) lets you send photos, videos, audio clips, and group messages to contacts who don’t use iMessage. It works over your cellular network, so you can reach Android and other non-Apple devices.


### How do I enable MMS on my iPhone?


Go to Settings → Messages → MMS Messaging, then toggle it On. If you don’t see the option, your carrier may not support MMS or it may be disabled on your plan.


### Why does my phone say “MMS messaging needs to be enabled?”


That message appears when your iPhone tries to send a picture or video but MMS is turned off or unsupported by your carrier. Turn on MMS Messaging and Send as SMS, then try again on cellular data.


### Do I need to turn off iMessage to send MMS?


No. iMessage and MMS work side by side. iMessage sends between Apple devices; MMS handles media messages to everyone else.


### Why won’t my MMS send on Wi-Fi?


Some carriers block MMS over Wi-Fi Calling. Turn off Wi-Fi Calling, resend over cellular, and then re-enable Wi-Fi if needed.
